items.titleTR: Jayden Daniels should blame coaching decision for compounding impact of Commanders miscues

slots.packetSpot: Dallas rebounded offensively against a depleted Washington after the disappointing defeat in the first week. Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels reportedly dislocated his left elbow; while the severity of the injury remains unclear, questions are growing around Washington’s season and quarterback plan.
slots.packetTitle: Dallas finds its footing as Washington waits

items.descriptionTR: Nigeria's government has appointed a 10-member independent panel to investigate the deaths of 37 people while they were held in custody on suspicion of illegal gold-mining in Niger state.
items.titleTR: Nigeria names panel to probe deaths of 37 miners held in detention

items.descriptionTR: Authorities linked the deaths to disease, but this has been disputed by intelligence reports and relatives of the accused.
items.titleTR: Dozens of suspected illegal miners die in Nigerian custody

items.descriptionTR:
Police fire teargas as protests break out in city of Minna after deaths of suspected illegal goldminers, many of whom were children
Survivors from a prison cell in Nigeria where 37 suspected illegal goldminers died while in the custody of a paramilitary group this week have recounted their panic and struggle for breath, as police on Friday fired teargas at people protesting against the deaths and imposed an overnight curfew in the city of Minna.
The victims – many of whom were children – were found dead on Thursday in the cells of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), which had raided suspected illegal goldmines and ⁠locked up dozens of miners in the city, the state capital of the mineral-rich state of Niger.
items.titleTR: Survivors recount panic and struggle to breathe in Nigerian prison cell where 37 died

slots.packetSpot:
The deaths of 37 people held under NSCDC custody in Minna, the capital of Niger State, on suspicion of illegal gold mining are under investigation. The NSCDC’s initial statement cited a possible disease outbreak; the agency’s headquarters said the cause of death had not yet been determined.

An intelligence report shared with AFP raised the possibility of overcrowding and inadequate ventilation. According to survivors’ accounts, the cell was cramped, those inside struggled to breathe and called for help; the BBC could not independently verify these accounts. Another survivor said a substance that burned the throat and nose was sprayed into the cell.

The government appointed an independent 10-member panel; it is expected to submit its report on responsibility, negligence and possible abuses within two weeks. Twenty NSCDC officers and guards were suspended; the state commander was also reportedly suspended or taken into custody. Reports emerged that tear gas was used, live rounds were fired and there were deaths among protesters in Minna after demonstrations by relatives, miners and city residents; these details remain unclear.
slots.packetTitle: The unanswered questions behind 37 deaths in Minna

items.descriptionTR: Raids, arrests and internet restrictions imposed to ‘protect the family’ have persecuted LGBTQ+ groups while also hitting independent journalists and human rights organisations reporting on the police operation. Raids, arrests and internet restrictions imposed to ‘protect the family’ have persecuted LGBTQ+ groups while also hitting independent journalists and human rights organisations reporting on the police operation.
items.titleTR: Turkey Stages Wide-Ranging LGBT Crackdown for ‘Family Safety’

slots.packetSpot:
Pressure targeting LGBTQI+ organisations and individuals in Türkiye is reported to be widening. According to the report, coordinated police raids that began on Saturday targeted nine organisations; by Thursday, courts in various provinces had remanded at least 82 people in custody pending trial. Justice Minister Akın Gürlek said action had been taken against 162 people, nine associations and 13 businesses in 15 provinces.

The raids are reported to have affected clubs, cafés and homes as well as organisations, with SPoD and KAOS GL among them. Those detained include LGBTQI+ activists and members of rights organisations, while there are also people facing prostitution, drug and other charges; it is stated that not everyone detained was targeted because of advocacy for gay rights. Authorities reportedly used the obscenity law, while Gürlek was reported to have defended the actions and called for investigations to be increased.

More than 100 people, including journalists, were detained at a protest outside Istanbul's main courthouse and later released. The United Nations human rights office, the European Union, international human rights groups and civil society actors in Türkiye criticised or condemned the practices. Protests are also reported to have been held outside Türkiye's embassies in Paris, Brussels, London, Oslo and Washington.
slots.packetTitle: The narrowing space for LGBTQI+ people in Türkiye

items.descriptionTR: In July, MPs in the Assemblée Nationale approved the bill, which says that any law enforcement official who uses force is assumed to have acted legally in using their weapon. It now faces a vote in the Sénat.
items.titleTR: Thousands march in Paris against bill granting police presumption of legitimate self defense

slots.packetSpot:
Thousands of people in France marched in Paris and other cities on September 20 against a bill that would presume law enforcement officers acted lawfully when using their weapons. The bill, approved by National Assembly deputies in July, is now awaiting a Senate vote.

Politicians, rights groups and activists have voiced concern that the bill could increase police violence or impunity and could reverse the burden of proof in such cases. Those defending the bill say it would prevent officers who use armed force from automatically being treated as suspects or taken into custody.

The counter-petition on the National Assembly’s website reportedly collected 730,000 signatures, but was rejected by the Assembly’s legal affairs committee in July. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez called on police to be especially careful ahead of the protests; in Rennes, authorities said eight people were taken into custody after objects were thrown at police, and three police officers were injured.
slots.packetTitle: Accountability in the shadow of the gun

items.descriptionTR: President Trump and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D) are set to meet Monday at Gracie Mansion, the mayor’s house in the Big Apple, a White House official and the mayor’s press office said Sunday. In an emailed statement, Mamdani’s press office said that “the meeting will focus on issues affecting New York City…
items.titleTR: Trump, Mamdani to meet in New York on Monday

slots.packetSpot:
According to information provided by a White House official and Zohran Mamdani’s press office, US President Donald Trump and New York Mayor Mamdani are scheduled to meet at Gracie Mansion on Monday. The mayor’s press office said the meeting would concern issues affecting New York and the city’s residents.

The relationship between Trump and Mamdani, who stand at opposite ends of the political spectrum, was described as notably warm in previous contacts. Mamdani had said he found the earlier meeting at the White House productive; he had stated that the possibility of building additional housing in New York was discussed. Trump, meanwhile, had criticised Mamdani in the past and called him a “communist.”
slots.packetTitle: A planned meeting at Gracie Mansion

items.descriptionTR:
•	Remco Evenepoel dominates men’s event in Montreal
	•	Marlen Reusser denies Zoe Backstedt in women’s race
Remco Evenepoel etched his name into the history books with a dominant fourth successive men’s world time-trial victory in Montreal on Sunday.
The 2024 Olympic champion came into the race as the overwhelming favourite and he did not disappoint. Evenepoel was already more than 30 seconds ahead of the rest by the second intermediate time check, just over halfway along the 39.2km (24.4 mile) route.
items.titleTR: Evenepoel wins fourth world time trial title in a row, Reusser retains her crown

slots.packetSpot:
At the world time trials in Montreal, Remco Evenepoel won the men's title for the fourth consecutive time. He reportedly finished the race around a minute ahead of Filippo Ganna, while Paul Seixas was third. In the women's event, Marlen Reusser retained her title, finishing 40 seconds ahead of Zoe Backstedt; Franziska Koch took third place.

With this result, Evenepoel is reported to have become the first cyclist to win four consecutive men's time trial world titles and to have matched Tony Martin and Fabian Cancellara's record of four titles overall.
slots.packetTitle: The summit that does not change in Montreal

items.descriptionTR:
•	GB pair win doubles match in straight sets
	•	Finals to be played in Bologna in November
Few people across London enjoyed a more soothing night’s sleep than Leon Smith on Saturday. After an ideal first day for his team in their Davis Cup qualifier against Ecuador, where his singles players handled business efficiently, the Great Britain captain had the luxury of calling upon one member of each of the two best doubles pairs in the world to close out the tie.
In just their second match as partners rather than rivals the world No 1, Henry Patten, and Neal Skupski, the US Open champion a week ago, played their roles to perfection as they convincingly sealed their place in the Davis Cup Final 8 with a clinical 6-3, 6-4 victory against Gonzalo Escobar and Diego Hidalgo, securing for Great Britain an unassailable 3-0 lead. Harry Wendelken, the British No 7, closed out the tie with a 6-2, 6-3 win against Angel Veliz in the dead rubber.
items.titleTR: Patten and Skupski take Great Britain past Ecuador to reach Davis Cup Final 8

slots.packetSpot:
Britain secured a place in the finals for the first time since 2023 by beating Ecuador 4-0 in a Davis Cup qualifier at the Copper Box Arena in London. The doubles match in which Henry Patten and Neal Skupski beat Gonzalo Escobar and Diego Hidalgo 6-3, 6-4 gave Britain an unassailable 3-0 lead after singles victories by Toby Samuel and Arthur Fery.

Harry Wendelken completed the best-of-five tie at 4-0 by beating Angel Veliz 6-2, 6-3. The Final 8 stage of the Davis Cup Finals will be held in Bologna from 24 to 29 November; hosts Italy qualified directly for the tournament.
slots.packetTitle: Britain's ticket to Bologna

items.descriptionTR: Kenya's Agnes Ngetich breaks the world record for a women-only half marathon as she wins gold at the World Road Running Championships in Copenhagen.
items.titleTR: Ngetich breaks women-only half-marathon record

slots.packetSpot:
According to the BBC, Kenya's Agnes Ngetich won gold in the women's-only half marathon at the World Road Running Championships in Copenhagen with a time of 1:05:15, improving the world record by one second. The previous record belonged to her compatriot Peres Jepchirchir, who won world half-marathon gold in 2020.

The time is a record in women’s-only races; the overall women’s half-marathon world record of 1:02:52, held by Ethiopia’s Letesenbet Gidey, remains separate. Ngetich said she would discuss her future with her coach and was considering returning to track racing for the 2027 World Athletics Championships.
slots.packetTitle: Ngetich's gold in Copenhagen

items.descriptionTR:
•	McCullum: Brook has ‘grown as captain and person’
	•	England begin ODI series against Sri Lanka this week
England’s white-ball coach, Brendon McCullum, was full of praise for the captain, Harry Brook, after Saturday’s eight-wicket victory over Sri Lanka completed a T20 series whitewash and took the side to No 1 in the world.
Brook, player of the T20 series against Sri Lanka, has now won 23 of his 26 completed games as captain. If he is not yet considered a suitable candidate as Test leader, the cap fits nicely in the smash and grab format.
items.titleTR: McCullum hails Brook’s captaincy as England move top of T20 world rankings

slots.packetSpot:
England beat Sri Lanka by eight wickets in the third T20 match at Old Trafford to complete the series 3-0. As a result, they reportedly returned to number one in the T20 world rankings, taking over from India.

Sri Lanka were restricted to 124 in 18.5 overs; England reached the target in 9.4 overs, having lost two wickets. Jos Buttler remained unbeaten on 62, while Harry Brook made 33. Sonny Baker took 2-17, Jofra Archer 2-23; Jamie Overton, meanwhile, conceded 15 runs in four overs and took one wicket.

Brendon McCullum praised Brook's captaincy. Since Brook took charge of the team in the summer of 2024, England have won 23 of the 26 completed T20 matches. New Test coach Stephen Fleming also watched the match.
slots.packetTitle: England back on top in T20s

items.descriptionTR:
Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso criticised his players' game management after they were humbled 3-0 at Brentford, while defender Levi Colwill said his team were bullied at set pieces.
Brentford scored three second-half goals to ease past Chelsea, with Jaidon Anthony, Igor Thiago and Fabio Carvalho all scoring.
It was the third successive Premier League game in which Chelsea failed to win, having lost to Arsenal and drawn with Hull City last weekend.
While Chelsea have looked a threat in attack in their previous games, scoring 10 goals, defensively they look less than solid, with the three goals conceded at Brentford meaning they have been breached 12 times already.
Alonso is only the sixth manager to concede two or more goals in each of his first five Premier League matches in charge.
"I would say that we have dropped our consistency, our competitive mentality needed in the second half," Alonso said.
"I'm disappointed at the end with the second half and the result," Alonso said.
"This is not enough to compete in the Premier League, not to be able to go for the 90 minutes. This is why today we were punished. It's not about talking or looking for excuses."
"You know that the small details can be decisive. You don't have to give advantage in these kind of games. But it's about 95 minutes and we have not been able to keep that level throughout these few games in the start of the season and it's something that we'll have to do better."
Colwill said on Sky Sports that Chelsea were being "bullied" at set pieces. "It was tough. Maybe we overexposed ourselves [at 1-0 down] and they hit us on the counter-attack, which they're so good at," Colwill said.
"Second half we weren't good enough. We've got a lot to work on over the international break. Maybe at times we've been bullied [at set-pieces] and we have to improve at that. We can't rely on our front three to pull us of danger; we all need to help each other. We've got a lot of room to improve."
Alonso agreed with his captain, saying: "It's not just set pieces, but in duels, defence, in build-up, in and when we conceded first, but still we were in the game; but when you lose shape, you are out of control.
"So to be able to understand the game, to know what it takes to be competing until the end, is a process. It takes time for them to feel that. And at the moment we are not feeling it fully to compete for the whole game."
Keith Andrews LOVED @BrentfordFC's 3-0 win against Chelsea! ❤️ pic.twitter.com/TpGupnZKrF
— Premier League (@premierleague) September 18, 2026
Victory means Brentford remain unbeaten in the league heading into the international break, having won twice and drawn three.
"I was really looking forward to the game – the opposition have been setting up in a respectful way to nullify what we do," said Brentford boss Keith Andrews.
"I felt there was a performance bubbling, the approach was focused and in the second half we showed what we are. There's a really nice connection between the fans and players. We're enjoying the journey we're on. I love feeling that energy and how we play. We need to consistently evolve how we play."
The win moved Brentford up to third on nine points while Chelsea remain seventh on seven points.
items.titleTR: Bully boys: Brentford expose Chelsea's defensive woes

slots.packetSpot:
Brentford's 3-0 victory over Chelsea came in the second half. The result, shaped by goals from Jaidon Anthony, Igor Thiago and Fabio Carvalho, meant Chelsea failed to win for the third league match in a row following their defeat to Arsenal and draw with Hull City.

Chelsea have conceded 12 goals in five Premier League matches and remained seventh on seven points. Brentford, meanwhile, moved up to third on nine points and preserved their unbeaten record with two wins and three draws.

Xabi Alonso said he found his team's second-half consistency, game management and ability to compete for 90 minutes insufficient. Levi Colwill said they had struggled physically at set pieces, while Alonso pointed to shortcomings in defence, duels and build-up play, as well as the team's loss of shape. Keith Andrews said the second-half performance reflected the team's approach and its connection with the supporters.
slots.packetTitle: Brentford's second-half surge

items.descriptionTR:
The enigmatic tiger cats of South America now encompass a new species – the tilcayo – bringing the number of known tiger cat species to five
￼

The tilcayo (Leopardus tilcayo) in an animal refuge in La Paz, Bolivia
Paola Nogales-Ascarrunz
A new cat species has been scientifically described – the diminutive, spotted tilcayo from Bolivia.
Several species of small cat in the Leopardus genus live in South America, including the ocelot, margay, kodkod, Geoffroy’s cat and the tiger cat or oncilla. The similar appearance of these nocturnal and hard-to-spot cats has made separating them into distinct species difficult.
This is particularly true of tiger cats, which are about the size of a house cat, and are found in Costa Rica in Central America, and across a vast swathe of South America including Bolivia, Brazil, Venezuela, Colombia, Ecuador and Peru. Historically, there have been many local and scientific names for them, but they all got subsumed into a single species, Leopardus tigrinus.
Advertisement

Read more
Tiny orange frog around the size of a pencil tip is brand-new species
Genetic studies have since divided the species into four, resurrecting three of the species names that scientists once used before they were all lumped together under the name L. tigrinus. This process saw the official recognition of the southern tiger cat (Leopardus guttulus) in 2013, Leopardus emiliae in 2017 and the clouded tiger cat (Leopardus pardinoides) in 2024.
Now, Eduardo Eizirik at the Pontifical Catholic University of Rio Grande do Sul (PUCRS) in Porto Alegre, Brazil, and his colleagues have analysed the complete genomes of 38 individuals from the Leopardus genus, including 26 tiger cats from across their known range.
The genomics revealed a fifth distinct species living in the Bolivian Yungas forests on the east slopes of the Andes mountains. The researchers describe it under a completely new name: Leopardus tilcayo, naming it after the local term used for this cat.
Subscriber-only newsletter
Sign up to Editor’s Highlights

Sign up to newsletter
￼
“We’ve discovered a new species of cat that had not been scientifically named before,” says Eizirik, adding that this is the first time this has happened for a century.
“There are more cat species. Who can’t love that?” says Leslie Lyons at the University of California, Davis. “They’re hard to find and see, so it’s not surprising that some of the early taxonomy needs to be modified now we have more data.”
L. tilcayo has a combined head and body length of between about 42 and 50 centimetres and weighs between 1.5 and 2 kilograms. The genomes revealed that it diverged from the lineage containing L. tigrinus and L. pardinoides nearly 1.4 million years ago.
￼
Origin story of domestic cats rewritten by genetic analysis
Domestic cats originated in North Africa and spread to Europe in the past 2000 years, according to DNA evidence, while in China a different species of cat lived alongside people much earlier
Telling the new species apart visually is not easy. “The five tiger cat species are all cryptic species. They’re morphologically very similar,” says team member Jonas Lescroart at University of Antwerp in Belgium.
The researchers also found that in the Peruvian Yungas forests, on the west side of the Andes, there is a distinct group of cats in the L. tigrinus lineage that they describe as a novel subspecies, L. tigrinus antisuyo.
There are so many barriers in South America that can geographically isolate animal populations from each other, including mountains and rivers, that more cat species may be waiting to be found, says Lyons. “It’d be rather cool if we could find another species out there.”
L. tigrinus is listed as vulnerable by the IUCN Red List, but the new species and subspecies will have to be evaluated and protected as distinct units, says Eizirik, especially as the forests they live in are shrinking as agriculture expands.
Journal Reference:
Current Biology DOI: 10.1016/j.cub.2026.08.059
items.titleTR: Beautiful new cat species is first to be named in a century

slots.packetSpot:
A small wildcat living in Bolivia’s Yungas forests has been formally described as Leopardus tilcayo in a study published in Current Biology. The researchers retained the name tilcayo used by local communities; they said it is the first living cat species to be formally named in more than a century.

Genetic data from 38 cats sampled across several South American countries indicate that the tiger cats comprise five genetically distinct species. The tilcayo lineage is estimated to have diverged from the others about 1.4 million years ago. The animal, about 46 centimetres long and weighing 1.4 kilograms, has irregular rosettes on its light-brown fur.

Knowledge of tilcayo’s way of life remains limited. Faecal samples suggest that small rodents may be among its foods, while camera traps suggest that it may be more active at night. The researchers also identified a new tiger cat subspecies in Peru’s Yungas region and shared their findings with the IUCN, which is expected to assess the lineages separately. The Yungas forests, meanwhile, reportedly face pressure from deforestation, agricultural expansion, human-caused fires and mining.
slots.packetTitle: The forest’s hidden cat

items.descriptionTR:
•	Third baseman was standing near on-deck circle
	•	Player taken to hospital for X-rays and CT scan
Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman was taken to the hospital for tests after being struck in the face by a foul ball while standing in front of the on-deck circle during Sunday’s game against the Cincinnati Reds.
There was no immediate decision on whether Bregman, who was taken for X-rays and CT scans, would travel with the team back to Chicago after the Cubs’ 9-1 win.
items.titleTR: ‘A terrible, terrible accident’: Cubs’ Bregman undergoing CT scans after taking foul ball to face

slots.packetSpot:
Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman was taken to the hospital after a foul ball struck him in the face while he was standing near the Cubs' warm-up area in the fourth inning of the Cincinnati Reds game. Bregman left the field accompanied by a trainer after Michael Busch fouled off a pitch from Reds pitcher Luis Mey; X-rays and a CT scan were reportedly taken.

Craig Counsell said the blow landed on his left cheekbone, below the eye; Bregman had bleeding from his nose and swelling on his face. Bregman later shared a photo showing his swollen eye and blood on his cheek, saying he would return. The Cubs hoped he would be able to return to Chicago that night; hospital results were pending.
slots.packetTitle: A foul ball to Bregman's face

Authorities ban anti-immigration march after fireworks and other projectiles thrown at officers in city centre park
Dutch riot police dispersed several hundred far-right protesters in The Hague on Saturday after violence erupted and local authorities banned a planned march in the city against immigration and asylum policies.
The Dutch public broadcaster NOS reported that 24 people had been arrested, after some protesters threw fireworks and other projectiles at police.
items.titleTR: Dutch riot police break up violent far-right protest in The Hague

slots.packetSpot: A far-right march planned in The Hague against immigration and asylum policies was banned after violence broke out at the Malieveld; the municipality later ordered the crowd to disperse. Dutch riot police dispersed several hundred demonstrators. According to NOS, 24 people were detained. Some demonstrators reportedly threw fireworks and other objects at police; pepper spray and water cannons were also reportedly used. Justice Minister David van Weel said the demonstrators gave Nazi salutes, chanted antisemitic slogans and attacked police.
slots.packetTitle: The far right dispersed in The Hague

items.descriptionTR:
"Italian children cannot feel like a minority in the classroom," the country’s PM said Sunday.
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said her government is preparing two legislative proposals that would ban face coverings in Italian schools and restrict the number of foreign students allowed in classrooms.
“Italian children cannot feel like a minority in the classroom,” she said Sunday in a speech at Fenix, an annual event organized by the youth division of her right-wing Brothers of Italy party.
“If the number of children who do not understand the language of instruction becomes large, or even forms the majority, that is no longer integration; that is neglect,” Meloni added.
Roughly 930,000 students without Italian citizenship are enrolled in the country’s schools, representing almost 11.6% of the school population, according to research institute Fondazione ISMU.
Over the last decade, the number of foreign minors in the country has fallen by 4.5%, ISMU found.
Meloni did not elaborate on what her cabinet’s proposed cap on foreign students might entail.
The Italian leader came to power buoyed by voters concerned with immigration issues, and made tackling migration a key pillar of her campaign.
It’s not the first time Meloni’s government has looked to ban face coverings. In 2025 her party said it had plans to ban the burqa and niqab in all public spaces nationwide, calling the legislation a response to “Islamic separatism.” The bill is still under consideration in the country’s lower house.
items.titleTR: Meloni promises to ban veils in Italian schools and limit foreign students

slots.packetSpot:
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said at a gathering of Brothers of Italy's youth wing in Rome that she wants burqas and niqabs banned in schools, a legal limit imposed on the number of foreign students in classrooms, and Italian-language classes made compulsory for the parents of foreign students who have serious difficulty integrating into the school system. For these measures to become law, they first require government approval and then parliamentary approval within 60 days.

In Italy, garments that completely cover the face are not explicitly banned. However, a 1975 law prohibits helmets and clothing that make identification more difficult without a justified reason; a 2008 ruling states that full-face coverings may be worn for religious or cultural reasons provided the face is shown when an identity check is required. A burqa covers the entire face, including the eyes, while a niqab leaves the eyes uncovered.

A 30% limit on the proportion of foreign students per class and school is already in force; Meloni did not explain how this would change. Foreign students are reported to account for around 12% of school enrolments in Italy. The League, also part of the governing coalition, submitted a proposal this year that would ban helmets and clothing that make identification more difficult, except in specific circumstances such as sporting events and places of worship.
slots.packetTitle: Meloni's line on fitting in at school

items.descriptionTR:
The Sporting Tribune's Fernando Ramirez writes about how the Chargers offense has been so bad they sit at 0-2 with more questions than answers but the team believes they can fix it.
￼
Sep 20, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert (10) reacts after a play against the Las Vegas Raiders during the second half at SoFi Stadium.
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- The best indication of how the first two games have gone for the Chargers offense came with 2:24 left in the third quarter, facing 3rd-and-1 from their own 32-yard line.
Tre Harris came in motion as center Jake Slaughter snapped the ball with Harris moving behind him, but the ball hit the ground. Quarterback Justin Herbert fell on top of it, and the Chargers were forced to punt.
Herbert was fuming after the play, yelling as he walked toward the sideline. He sat next to quarterbacks coach Shane Day and was still visibly frustrated.
“I think it was because it was a big play for us and we didn’t execute,” Herbert said. “And that’s something I have to do a better job at.”
That play was a perfect example of what the Chargers offense has looked like through two games, which has led to an 0-2 start after their 26-14 loss to the Raiders.
Harris said the snap was “a little late” and he tried to jump on it, but the mistake killed the drive.
“It was unfortunate what happened,” Harris said.
Mistakes, fumbles, lack of awareness, dropped passes, interceptions and penalties. The Chargers have dealt with a little bit of everything.
The question now is: Is this fixable?
“It’s not to our standard,” Herbert said. “It’s on us to be better. We know what we’re capable of doing.”
The quarterback said more than his head coach.
“The competitors, the fight-when your backs against the wall, you have to fight your way out,” Jim Harbaugh said.
Harbaugh did say multiple times during his press conference that he is “not deterred” by the offensive start, and multiple players said they believe they can fix it.
There have been glimpses of what this offense can look like. There are positives, but through the first two games, it has mostly been a mess.
The offense was supposed to take the next step under Mike McDaniel, but instead, it looks like it has taken 10 steps back. This offense is unrecognizable from what was expected entering the season.
“Not good enough from any standpoint,” Chargers receiver Ladd McConkey said. “Offense it's got to be better. We got to score more points. Take care of the ball. So yeah, just not good enough.”
On their third offensive drive, the Chargers went three-and-out, but in a different way.
￼
Sep 20, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh looks on against the Las Vegas Raiders during the first half at SoFi Stadium.
Kirby Lee-Imagn Images
Sep 20, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Los Angeles Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh looks on against the Las Vegas Raiders during the first half at SoFi Stadium.
Herbert faced 3rd-and-5 from his own 22 when he threw a pass to David Njoku, who appeared to have it before bobbling the ball. Raiders cornerback Hezekiah Masses intercepted it and returned it to the Chargers’ 23-yard line.
If Njoku catches it, he has a big gain. Instead, it became another turnover. It ultimately didn’t cost the Chargers points thanks to the defense, which held the Raiders on four straight plays from the two-yard line to give the offense the ball back.
“Frustrated, you know,” Chargers left tackle Rashawn Slater said. “We clearly have everything we're capable of doing out there. Coming close, but we're not finishing drives. We're so many self-inflicted wounds. We're shooting ourselves in the foot. You're never gonna win like that, so we get we need to fix that.”
Two offensive drives later, the Chargers had the ball at their own two-yard line but couldn’t muster much offensively. On 3rd-and-5, right tackle Joe Alt committed two straight false-start penalties, turning it into 3rd-and-9 before the Chargers handed the ball to Omarion Hampton.
“Of course, you want to win,” Alt said. “That's why we play football. You want to win. So, you never want to lose. That's the worst part about you know worst part of the sport is losing. So you want to go back to work and improve.”
On their next offensive drive, there was finally a glimpse of hope.
On 3rd-and-11 from their own 30, Herbert found McConkey for a 19-yard gain. Two plays later, Herbert was being pulled down by a Raiders defender when he got a pass off to Hampton, who picked up 18 yards.
On 1st-and-10 from the Raiders’ 11, Hampton bullied his way to the one-yard line. On the next play, he punched it in for a one-yard touchdown to tie the game at 7-7.
At halftime, Raiders receiver Tre Tucker had 68 receiving yards. The entire Chargers offense had 55 total yards.
That is how ugly it has been.
“We know the players we have,” McConkey said. “Just got to execute. Like we're really hurting ourselves. Turnovers, penalties, drops, like whatever it may be. We're hurting ourselves. So just got to clean that up, execute, and I think we'll be okay.”
The Chargers’ most encouraging drive came to start the second half.
After leaning heavily on Hampton following a 70-rushing-yard first half, the Chargers faced 3rd-and-5 from their own 42. Herbert found a wide-open Harris downfield for a 53-yard gain, taking the offense to the Raiders’ five-yard line.
Two plays later, Herbert found tight end Oronde Gadsden for a 10-yard touchdown to give the Chargers their first lead of the game, 14-10.
The Raiders answered with a long drive of their own.
On 3rd-and-10 from their own 26, Cousins found Tucker for a nine-yard gain, followed by a one-yard “Tush Push” from fullback Connor Heyward for the first down. Four plays later, Jeanty took a handoff and threw it back to Cousins, who found receiver Dareke Young for a 27-yard gain.
On 3rd-and-10 from the Chargers’ 13, Cousins found receiver Cody White in the end zone for a 13-yard touchdown to put the Raiders ahead 17-14.
The Chargers defense then forced back-to-back punts, giving the offense opportunities to respond.
On the fifth play of the ensuing drive, Alt was called for his third false start of the game, setting up 2nd-and-15. The Chargers eventually converted, but on the following play, Hampton ran for two yards before Nakobe Dean forced a fumble. Raiders safety Jeremy Chinn recovered and returned it to the Chargers’ 16-yard line.
“I have got to be better,” Hampton said.
￼
Sep 20, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Las Vegas Raiders safety Jeremy Chinn (11) recovers a fumble against the Los Angeles Chargers during the second half at SoFi Stadium.
Gary A. Vasquez-Imagn Images
Sep 20, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Las Vegas Raiders safety Jeremy Chinn (11) recovers a fumble against the Los Angeles Chargers during the second half at SoFi Stadium.
It was a mirror image of last week’s blocked punt. Once again, a mistake put the defense in a terrible spot and ultimately gave away a touchdown.
Cousins found White in the end zone for an 11-yard score, his second receiving touchdown of the game, putting the Raiders ahead 24-14 and delivering what felt like the final blow.
“I think it's just going out there and making sure that we have a game next week and got to be at our best for that game because they're a very good team and there's nothing we can do to change the past two weeks,” Herbert said. “So it's on us to fix our stuff, make sure that we’re ready to go for next week.”
The team waiting next week?
The 2-0 Buffalo Bills. In Buffalo.
The Bills are averaging 39 points per game on offense while the Chargers are averaging 14. This “high-powered” McDaniel offense has scored four touchdowns through two games against teams that had top picks in last year’s draft.
“We got to look each other in the eye, man, and just tell the truth and just get better,” James said. “Because right now that shit just looks trash.”
It now falls on Harbaugh, McDaniel and the offense to figure out how to fix it. The defense has caught some flak, but it has largely held down the fort while repeatedly being put in difficult situations because of turnovers and other mistakes.
“It's right there for us,” Khalil Mack said. “We feel like we doing a lot of things to hurt ourselves right now, and once we get those things fixed, it'll look a lot better.”
All three phases are being honest about the fact that the Chargers aren’t playing up to their standard two games into the season.
The roughest part is what comes next. Their next seven games are against some of the NFL’s toughest competition.
They just faced two of the perceived “lower-tier” teams on their schedule and were outscored 52-28.
How they fix this is anyone’s guess, but through the first two games, the offense has failed to produce the results that were expected. That is a major reason why the Chargers sit at 0-2.
“We'll go back to work, that’s all I know how to do,” Harbaugh said. “That's all we know how to do, find the way, and we'll move forward.”
items.titleTR: Harbaugh, McDaniel searching for answers as Chargers fall to 0-2

slots.packetSpot:
The Las Vegas Raiders’ 26-14 victory over the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood on September 20 moved the Raiders to 2-0 while leaving the Chargers at 0-2. Expectations for the AFC West at the start of the season were shaken by the result, while the main question in Los Angeles is how the offense will recover.

Turnovers, fumbles, dropped passes, interceptions, penalties and execution errors stood out on the Chargers’ side. Justin Herbert and Jim Harbaugh said the team needs to be better, while players said they believe the problems can be fixed. The report says the defense often limited the damage despite the difficult situations created by the offense’s mistakes.

The Chargers’ next opponent is the 2-0 Buffalo Bills in Buffalo. The report states that the Bills are averaging 39 points per game, compared with 14 for the Chargers; Los Angeles will take the field in Buffalo next week.
slots.packetTitle: Early AFC West calculations unravel

items.descriptionTR: Jaylen Waddle broke out as Denver rallied from a 10-point third-quarter deficit to beat Jacksonville at Empower Field.
items.titleTR: Bo Nix brings Broncos back from brink. Did Denver figure things out vs. Jaguars?

items.descriptionTR:
The Jacksonville Jaguars lost a game to the Denver Broncos because they forgot Liam Coen's mantra of playing "complementary football"
The Jacksonville Jaguars' 20-13 loss to the Denver Broncos on Sept. 20 at Empower Field at Mile High was, in a way, a death by a thousand cuts.
Well, hardly a thousand. But there were no highlight-reel plays, devastating in-game injuries, or one opposing player dominating the game that led to the Jags' first loss in their last 10 regular-season games.
Denver didn't rally from 19 points down in the final period, as Houston did last year. The Broncos didn't stage a 92-yard scoring drive late in the game to come from behind, as Cincinnati did last year. And they didn't blow the Jags out, as the Los Angeles Rams did last year.
What happened to the Jaguars in Denver was a series of events that individually weren't game-changing, but stacked on each other, turned a 13-3 lead and a crowd that seemed to go pouty en masse into every NFL team's fear: Momentum, with the volume turned up to the max.
A lot of it came because the Jaguars didn't practice what coach Liam Coen preaches: Situational and complementary football.
Whether it was the special teams allowing good field position on two Denver scores, Trevor Lawrence's first interception in eight games when the offense was driving at midfield, or the Broncos running the ball effectively in the fourth quarter with their third-team back, a rookie drafted in the fourth round, Denver kept building on each sequence until it had the lead and was in the victory formation.
￼
The good news is that it's only Week 2 and the issues are fixable before the New England Patriots come to town Sept. 27 at EverBank Stadium (CBS, 1 p.m.).
"I'm proud of the team in terms of the effort," Coen said during his post-game radio show. "I don't think we let our foot off the gas in terms of the way we were calling it, the way we were operating. We just got to find a way to make a play."
Brian Thomas Jr. drops rear their ugly head again
One of the things that stalled the offense was the return of the slippery substance on the hands of wide receiver Brian Thomas Jr. Thomas didn't drop sure touchdown passes in the end zone. There was plenty of time left in the game after the second drop.
But it wasn't a good sign for a player who battled ball security issues last season.
Thomas' first drop came on a first-down play from the Jaguars' 38, after Parker Washington returned a punt 12 yards. Had Thomas caught the ball, it would have been a gain of at least 6 yards and perhaps more.
￼
The second drop came in the fourth quarter, one play after Lawrence and Jakobi Meyers connected on a 28-yard pass to the Broncos 38 after Denver had tied the game 13-13. If Thomas catches the ball, the Jaguars have a first down at the Denver 25.
Trevor Lawrence's interception
It was only one turnover, and it was Lawrence's second in eight games. But even having to punt in that situation would have been better.
With a 13-6 lead, the Jaguars had a third-and-six at midfield with the end of the third quarter winding down. Lawrence underthrew a pass to Washington (seven receptions, 98 yards), who was well-covered by Riley Moss, and failed to see Meyers open over the middle on a crossing pattern.
After taking possession, Bo Nix busted two chunk plays to tight end Nate Adkins and Jaylen Waddle and then tied the game on a 7-yard TD pass to Adkins.
Denver wins field position battle
Two Denver scores were the result of getting short fields.
The Jaguars took a 7-0 lead early in the second quarter on an efficient 72-yard drive in which Lawrence completed all four of his passes for 65 yards and Bhayshul Tuten scored on a 1-yard run on a direct snap.
But Tyler Badie returned the kickoff 38 yards to the Denver 40. The Broncos drove to the 1-yard line, failed to get in the end zone on three plays and settled for a Will Lutz field goal.
Denver then scored the winning touchdown with 7:21 left on Jonah Coleman's 3-yard run, a drive that began at the Broncos' 44 after Cam Little missed a 54-yard field-goal attempt. Cornerback Travis Hunter had a tough time on the possession, getting beat on a 17-yard completion to former Jaguar Evan Engram and then getting flagged for pass interference.
The latter play led to a flag on Coen for arguing too vehemently, or perhaps too colorfully in terms of his vocabulary. Coleman scored on the next play.
Jags don't get in the end zone
The Jaguars took the crowd completely out of the game while moving downfield to start the third quarter, and had first-and-goal at the 3.
Some of the Jags' old goal-line issues then resurfaced.
Chris Rodriguez was thrown for a 2-yard loss when the left side of the Jaguars' line caved in, Lawrence threw a pass to Tuten that resulted in no gain, and he then failed to see Brenton Strange open on the left and threw the ball over the middle to LeQuint Allen Jr., short of the goal line, with two Denver defenders there to keep him out of the end zone. The ball was jarred loose, and the Jags had to take the 23-yard Little field goal.
At the time, 13-3 seemed like a nice consolation prize. But 17-3, in retrospect, sounds better.
Rookie running back closes the game
Denver's starting running back, R.J. Harvey, was declared out before the game with a hamstring injury. His replacement, J.K. Dobbins, was little of a factor with 36 yards (15 on one play) before he was injured near the end of the third quarter on a 4-yard gain.
￼
Left for the Broncos was Coleman, a rookie drafted in the fourth round who didn't get a carry in the opening game. But he scored the tie-breaking touchdown from 3 yards out, then gained 33 yards on Denver's final possession that ate up the final 4:41 of the game. Coleman broke off two 12-yard gains on the possession to pick up first downs, the last on second-and-11.
This article originally appeared on Florida Times-Union: Jaguars lose track of 'complementary football' in loss to Broncos
items.titleTR: Jaguars lose track of 'complementary football' in loss to Broncos

slots.packetSpot:
The Denver Broncos beat the Jacksonville Jaguars 20-13 at Empower Field at Mile High on September 20. Jacksonville's 13-3 lead eroded not through a single decisive play, but through a succession of missed opportunities and mistakes.

Trevor Lawrence's interception on third down at midfield, Brian Thomas Jr.'s two dropped passes, settling for a field goal rather than a touchdown at the goal line, and Cam Little's missed 54-yard field goal limited Jacksonville's chances of regaining momentum. Denver tied the score on Bo Nix passes to Nate Adkins and Jaylen Waddle; rookie Jonah Coleman's 3-yard touchdown put them ahead. Coleman also helped run down the remaining 4 minutes and 41 seconds with the 33 yards he gained on the final drive.

Liam Coen and Lawrence said after the game that they need to be better in situational and complementary play. Jacksonville's next opponent is the New England Patriots on September 27.
slots.packetTitle: Momentum swung Denver's way after 13-3

items.titleTR: Converse apologises and pulls sneaker ad that critics said included racist imagery

items.descriptionTR: The company earlier pulled the controversial advertisement and apologised for it publicly.
items.titleTR: Converse CEO pledges review over ad that critics say evoked KKK

slots.packetSpot:
Converse removed the Chuck 70 X advertisement featuring Karina from its channels and apologised. Critics argued that the white triangular shape created by the light and shadows on the skirt resembled a Ku Klux Klan hood, while the way the sneakers were held evoked the dangling feet of a lynched person. While acknowledging that the image should not have been used, the company said it was working to remove the advertisement from everywhere it had been published.

In a note sent to employees, Converse CEO Aaron Cain said they would review the internal review process and the critical approach applied to work, and make the necessary changes. The reactions also included calls for those involved in the advertisement to be fired and for the brand to be boycotted.

Ten lions were found dead in Tanzania’s Ngorongoro Conservation Area. The Ngorongoro Conservation Area Authority announced that initial findings indicated the animals may have ingested poison and that a comprehensive investigation had been launched to determine the cause of the incident and those responsible.

The area is also home to pastoral communities that raise cattle and is considered one of the country’s most visited tourist destinations. Paris Saint-Germain beat Marseille 2-1 in Le Classique at the Velodrome on Sunday, 20 September. Ferran Torres came on as a substitute and scored PSG's first goal in the 66th minute; Angel Gomes equalised six minutes later. PSG captain Marquinhos then scored the winner three minutes later.

items.descriptionTR:
The UN has passed a non-binding resolution to endorse the Equal Earth Projection, a map which more fairly represents the true size of the Earth’s landmasses. The current commonly used projection, called the Mercator Projection, greatly exaggerates land towards the north and south poles, which makes Africa look much smaller. In the Mercator projection, countries near the north and south pole can be anywhere from two to 14 times their true size. In the Equal Earth projection these distortions are minimised, making Africa look larger in comparison.
We asked Jack Swab and Derek Alderman, cartographers and geographers who study the social and communicative power of maps, to explain what’s going on.

What is a map projection?
A map projection is a technique that cartographers (map-makers) use to transform the round, three-dimensional Earth into a flat, two-dimensional map that we see on the wall or on our computer screen. As cartographers flatten the globe, the map becomes distorted, changing shapes and areas. There is no map projection that does not distort the Earth, but some projections are better suited for some uses than others.
A cartographer’s job is to choose from the hundreds of different map projections, and consider where the map is focused and how it is going to be used. No single projection is best for every use. This new Equal Earth projection is better suited than Mercator for producing global scale world maps for educational, public communication and policy purposes.
The Equal Earth supports a more accurate geographic understanding of the relative sizes of countries and continents. It provides a fairer perspective for the public to compare regions in terms of population, environment, development, politics and other global patterns.
Is the Mercator projection still useful?
While the Mercator projection isn’t good for showing the size of the Earth’s landmasses, we won’t see it totally disappear. For example, it’s very useful for navigational purposes as it maintains the accuracy of a compass bearing between two points without having to recalculate it.
This is why most online mapping platforms like Google Maps or Apple Maps rely on a variation of the Mercator projection to provide directions. Using the Equal Earth projection for navigation would not be as effective as the Mercator projection.
How will the Equal Earth projection be used?
Map-making is decentralised and there is no single authority regulating which map projection is used. What the UN did was endorse the broader message that Equal Earth is a fairer projection that more equitably displays the true size of the Earth’s land. And although this action is happening at a global level, there are movements underway in cartographic communities to make the Equal Earth projection the default world map projection.
The UN resolution by itself will not make Equal Earth a globally adopted projection. That requires intentional revision of maps used in textbooks, databases, media productions and diplomatic discussions, which requires labour and financial investment.
The Equal Earth projection was developed by cartographers and is a popular choice among map-makers since it was unveiled in 2018. It’s now possible to buy wall maps with the Equal Earth projection on them, and the projection has already been used in a wide variety of media. That said, individuals will need to opt in to using the Equal Earth projection over other types.
Why has the Equal Earth projection sparked resistance?
Resistance to the Equal Earth projection has been quite limited. There were several abstentions from the United Nations General Assembly vote, but most of this was for other reasons. Ukraine, for example, raised concerns over the depiction of the contested Crimean Peninsula on the map, which the Equal Earth Projection website depicts as contested territory.
This spurred a Russian response, along with points from other nations about contested territory. Given the UN resolution was a vote on how the world is portrayed and not about any specific political boundaries (a point that both Russia and Ukraine agreed on), these discussions amounted to geopolitical posturing about non-map issues.
The lone outlier, and only “no” vote against the Equal Earth projection, came from the United States. It claimed that the proposal was part of a “radical and ideological project” that was not appropriate for the United Nations to be debating. American delegates took issue with language linking Mercator’s distortions to colonial legacies and the marginalisation of Africa. This is not surprising since the current administration denies the existence of structural systems of inequality.
It is hard to miss the hypocrisy at play. The US wants other countries not to discuss the political implications of cartography even as President Trump engages in his own nationalist branding of the map. He has unilaterally renamed the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America and Lake Ontario to Lake America for clear ideological reasons and without international consultation.
How does the new map matter when it comes to changing global views of the world?
The argument that African nations put forward was that the Equal Earth projection is a form of “cognitive justice”. Cognitive justice recognises that people often equate power and value of places with their apparent size on maps. Traditional views of Africa as a smaller continent compared to Europe or North America typically reflect the perceived importance of these parts of the world.
Equal Earth may make it easier to teach, broadcast and discuss a different view of Africa and its prominence in the world. Today, African countries are among the world’s fastest growing economies and fastest growing populations. Map projections alone cannot change people’s attitudes. Yet, as African nations seek to have more influence in international affairs, correcting the mental map of global leaders is an important step in amplifying the continent’s relevance and rights.
￼
The authors do not work for, consult, own shares in or receive funding from any company or organisation that would benefit from this article, and have disclosed no relevant affiliations beyond their academic appointment.
Correcting the mental map of global leaders is an important step in amplifying Africa’s relevance and rights.
items.titleTR: New world map makes Africa look bigger: what’s the fuss about? Cartographers explain

slots.packetSpot:
The UN General Assembly’s resolution encouraging the use of Equal Earth and other equal-area map projections has brought renewed prominence to the debate over how Africa appears on world maps. The Correct the Map campaign, led by Togo, and the backing of the African Union converge with criticism that the Mercator projection makes the continent appear smaller than it is. The resolution was adopted with 164 votes, with the United States the only member voting against it.

Togolese Foreign Minister Robert Dussey described the outcome as a source of pride; he linked the cartographic debate to perceptions of Africa’s place in the world, identity, knowledge production and power relations. According to French historian Romain Tiquet, maps are part of the debate over the decolonisation of knowledge, which has extended from universities to museums and civil society since the late 2000s.

This trend is also visible in education. In October 2025, Mali decided to remove French history from the curriculum and place greater emphasis on Malian history and the former West African kingdoms. In Tanzania, the course “Tanzanian history and ethics” replaced the global history course, became compulsory and was planned to be taught in Swahili. Historian Philemon Mtoi stresses that knowledge of other countries and global history should not be erased, and that important events should be taught at later stages; he notes that similar approaches have been adopted in Ghana, Namibia, South Africa and Kenya.

Africa No Filter, meanwhile, works against portrayals of Africa as a continent that is poor, corrupt and in crisis. A report by the organisation estimates that biased media coverage could cost Africa up to $4.2 billion a year through inflated interest payments. Its #NotWaiting campaign aims to make initiatives and positive developments on the continent more visible; it also seeks to ensure that entrenched perceptions of Africa are questioned from within the continent.
slots.packetTitle: As Africa redraws its place

items.descriptionTR:
France is loaning the New Spain-era manuscript that chronicles the founding, splendor, and fall of Tenochtitlan to the National Museum of Anthropology and History
The Azcatitlan Codex, a 50‑folio summary of the Aztec empire’s history, has temporarily returned to Mexico on loan from France to mark the 200th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries. The document left Mexico in 1840 and has come back nearly two centuries later to be exhibited for three months at the National Museum of Anthropology and History in Mexico City. Mexican president Claudia Sheinbaum and French president Emmanuel Macron agreed in November 2025 to exchange this codex and the Boturini Codex to mark the relaunch of Franco‑Mexican relations.
Seguir leyendo
￼
items.titleTR: The Azcatitlan Codex returns to Mexico from Europe after nearly two centuries

slots.packetSpot:
The Azcatitlan Codex is on display at the National Museum of Anthropology and History in Mexico City, on a three-month loan from France nearly two centuries after leaving Mexico. The loan, tied to the 200th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Mexico and France, is part of an exchange agreement reportedly reached by Claudia Sheinbaum and Emmanuel Macron in November 2025, covering the Azcatitlan and Boturini codices.

The 50-folio manuscript, dated to the late 17th century, recounts the migration from Aztlán, the founding of Tenochtitlan, major events during the reigns of Aztec rulers, the arrival of the Spanish conquistadors in 1519, and the establishment of the caste system in New Spain. Held by the National Library of France since a donation by the Goupil family in 1896, the work will return to France in December; the Boturini Codex, displayed in Paris, will also be returned to Mexico that month.

Baltazar Brito Guadarrama, director of the National Library of Anthropology and History, says that although the codex was prepared at a late date, it offers important clues about the history of Aztec peoples. Culture Minister Claudia Curiel de Icaza says that some pages have been lost over time and that the content remains open to interpretation.
slots.packetTitle: A temporary return after nearly two centuries

According to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, he is scheduled to meet Donald Trump in New York this week. Zelensky described the phone call as important and said there was diplomatic momentum.

items.descriptionTR: Rising diesel prices are proving to be a particular problem for Republicans as surging energy costs sour the economic mood just 45 days out from the midterms.  The national average for diesel jumped 42 cents over the last week, largely as a result of the ongoing U.S. war in Iran, though President Trump has sought…
items.titleTR: Soaring diesel prices pose latest economic headache for GOP

items.descriptionTR:
Most Americans don't buy diesel, but the soaring costs of trucking and shipping goods have cost the average household $350.
Diesel prices hit an all-time high on Friday. Then another, and another. 
According to AAA, the average price of diesel as of September 10 stands at a staggering $5.98 — about $2.31 more than in late February, when the United States and Israel launched a war against Iran. The jump has been even higher in some states, such as California, where a gallon of diesel currently costs $7.91. 
Most Americans don’t buy diesel fuel, but they pay for it. It powers the trucks and ships that move everything from milk to lumber, and the costs are embedded in the prices people see at stores. The last time consumers saw diesel prices climb to such heights was in 2022, when Russia invaded Ukraine and they hit $5.82 per gallon. 
This year, the Iran war has largely closed the Strait of Hormuz, through which 10 percent of seaborne diesel once traveled. This has sent prices soaring, and consumers are increasingly feeling the impact. 
“Early on, much of the cost increase gets absorbed along the supply chain through existing freight contracts and retailer margins,” David Ortega, a professor of food economics and policy at Michigan State University, told the Associated Press. “But as contracts reprice and fuel surcharges take hold, more of that cost makes its way to the grocery store.” 
All told, the rising price of diesel has cost U.S. consumers an additional $46 billion, or about $350 per household, according to a Brown University tracker. That’s slightly less than the impact of rising gasoline prices — at $55 billion — but the 61 percent jump in diesel prices has outpaced the 41 percent increase in gas. 
“Diesel right now is caught up in more of a geopolitical turmoil than gasoline,” said Patrick De Haan, head of petroleum analysis for GasBuddy, an app that lets consumers track fuel prices. In addition to the Iran war, Ukraine’s increasingly successful attacks on Russian oil refineries have also applied upward pressure. 
“Russia is no longer supplying the global market,” said De Haan, and U.S. refineries are already at full capacity, giving them little ability to pick up the slack. Domestic inventories are at their lowest level since 1982, according to data from the Energy Information Administration.
“We’re entering a key period for diesel consumption with the lowest inventories on record for early September,” David Russell told Reuters. He’s the global head of market strategy at the brokerage service TradeStation. “Farmers and truckers typically use more diesel in the autumn, which raises the stakes for the current crisis and increases the risk of sharper price increases.” 
Winter is likely to bring more problems. Because heating oil is also essentially diesel, the millions of U.S. households that still rely on it can expect unprecedented bills. This comes as President Donald J. Trump’s administration has threatened to eliminate the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program, which helps households afford their fuel bills. 
“If you’re in the Northeast, then this is much more burdensome than anywhere else in the country,” Mark Wolfe, executive director of the National Energy Assistance Directors Association, told Axios. “Families are getting hit by both gasoline and heating oil.” 
These surging costs are hitting consumers just before the midterm elections, when the economy is at the front of voters’ minds. Normally, fuel prices are a somewhat downstream factor in the voting calculus, but Kevin Book, head of research at energy consulting firm ClearView Energy Partners, told Axios that this year could be different. “In cold weather states — particularly those that rely on fuels other than natural gas,” he said. “It could be a very big deal.”
Even if the wars in Iran and Ukraine were to end tomorrow, it would take weeks or months for fuel prices to come down and diesel supply to recover. 
“After both of those are solved, then once the flow normalizes, that will start to help global inventories recover,” said De Haan. “Only after inventories have recovered do diesel prices really see a full decline.”
This post has been updated to reflect the current price of diesel fuel as of September 10.
This story was originally published by Grist with the headline What the record-high cost of diesel means for you on Sep 10, 2026.
items.titleTR: What the record-high cost of diesel means for you

slots.packetSpot:
As diesel prices in the United States climb to record levels, two different national averages stand out: $6.27 per gallon in one measure, and $5.98 as of September 10 in another based on AAA data. The latter calculation states that the price has risen by about $2.31 since late February; in California, a gallon has reached $7.91.

The increase is linked to the U.S.-Israel war with Iran, disruption around the Strait of Hormuz, attacks on Russian oil refineries in connection with Ukraine, low U.S. inventories and limited refinery capacity. The rise in costs for diesel used in trucking, public transportation, agriculture, maritime transport and heating is expected to feed into consumer spending, including grocery prices, as freight contracts are renewed and fuel surcharges take effect. Brown University’s tracking study puts the additional cost at $46 billion for U.S. consumers, or about $350 per household.

Greater diesel use by farmers and truckers in the autumn could increase the pressure as winter approaches. The burden is said to be particularly heavy for Northeastern households dependent on heating fuel; the Trump administration’s threat to eliminate the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program is also reported to be on the agenda. Even if the wars in Iran and Ukraine end immediately, prices are reportedly not expected to fully decline within weeks or months without flows returning to normal and inventories recovering.

As the midterm elections approach, prices are also becoming an issue of economic pressure for Donald Trump and Republicans. Senate Majority Leader John Thune said he was open to examining a diesel export ban, while Interior Secretary Doug Burgum argued that such a ban would probably not lower prices. Republican and Democratic candidates are putting forward different political responses to rising energy costs.
slots.packetTitle: Diesel’s lingering shadow

items.descriptionTR: President Trump on Sunday speculated on the future of the Iran war, asking “if and when do I blow the entire nation up?” Fox News’s Trey Yingst reported that Trump is in a “deciding mode” and “that very big things are going to be happening in the not-so-distant future.” “The president described the current choices…
items.titleTR: Trump on Iran: ‘My question is, if and when do I blow the entire nation up?’

slots.packetSpot:
Donald Trump’s words as he weighs how to proceed in the Iran war bring the possibility of escalation to the fore. According to The Hill’s account citing Fox News correspondent Trey Yingst, Trump listed the options of destroying Iran, leaving it to decay economically, or reaching an agreement; he asked, “When am I going to blow up the whole country?”

Trump also said he was considering whether to move to “destroy” the Iranian regime. These remarks are reported not as a decision that has been made or an operation that has been launched, but as options voiced regarding the next phase of the war.
slots.packetTitle: Trump weighs Iran's ruin

items.descriptionTR: The State Department approved a potential $2.6 billion air defense equipment sale to Ukraine Friday as its conflict with Russia resumed following trilateral talks with U.S. special envoys.  In a congressional notification, the State Department wrote that the Ukrainian government requested S-300 Clone missiles, GAM-67 missiles, Range-Extended Air Defense Laser Guided Rocket missile systems, counter-drone…
items.titleTR: State Department approves potential $2.6B military air defense equipment sale to Ukraine

slots.packetSpot:
The US State Department has approved a possible $2.6 billion sale of air defence equipment to Ukraine. According to the notification to Congress, the requested items include S-300 Clone missiles, GAM-67 missiles, extended-range laser-guided air defence rocket systems, counter-drone radars, and logistics and programme support.

It was reported that the proposed purchase would be covered by European contributions and US Foreign Military Financing allocated during the previous administration. The US Embassy in Kyiv stated that the possible sale would strengthen Ukraine's air defence capacity for its self-defence and regional security missions.

The approval came after attempts at trilateral talks involving representatives of Moscow, Kyiv and the United States. Ukraine's Ministry of Defence reported that Russia had resumed attacks on targets in Kyiv and other major cities after the talks; the European Union's Ambassador to Ukraine, Katarína Mathernová, said that at least two people had been killed and 10 injured in the attacks. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had also requested additional air defence systems, particularly Patriot interceptors.
slots.packetTitle: A door opens over Ukraine

items.descriptionTR: It is the first time the juror, who refused to side with the others and acquit Clancy, has spoken publicly about his decision.
items.titleTR: Lindsay Clancy holdout juror says he had no doubt she deliberately killed her children

slots.packetSpot:
In the case in which Lindsay Clancy admitted to killing her three children, the jury failed to reach a unanimous verdict after approximately 40 hours of deliberation; a mistrial was declared on September 4. Michael Desronvil, the sole dissenting juror in the case, said he had no doubt, based on the physical evidence, witnesses and the prosecution’s presentation, that Clancy bore criminal responsibility and had planned the deaths.

While the defense argued that Clancy had experienced postpartum psychosis, the prosecution maintained that the deaths were calculated. Accounts from the other jurors indicate that the panel was split 11 to 1 in favor of finding that Clancy bore no criminal responsibility; accounts differ as to whether Desronvil accepted reasonable doubt.

The case has not been resolved. It has not been announced whether the prosecution will seek a retrial; the next hearing will be held on September 29 at Plymouth Superior Court in Massachusetts.
slots.packetTitle: One dissent, an unresolved case

items.descriptionTR: Ross Smith thrashed Gerwyn Price 11-5 to become World Series of Darts Finals champion, while Luke Littler's hopes of a clean sweep of all major PDC titles in 2026 were dashed in the quarter-finals.
items.titleTR: Smith thrashes Price to win World Series after Littler's shock exit

slots.packetSpot:
Ross Smith won the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam by beating Gerwyn Price 11-5. According to reports, Smith took the final six legs of the final, hit 11 maximums and produced two finishes above 100; it was his second PDC major title.

Luke Littler, meanwhile, lost 10-4 to Jonny Clayton in the quarter-finals. Littler, who was said to have won the year's first six PDC major tournaments, thereby saw his aim of winning all 11 majors in 2026 come to an end.

After the final, Price described his performance as “an absolute disgrace”; he said he would not care even if he never won another major.
slots.packetTitle: Smith at the summit, Littler's run cut short

items.descriptionTR: Ireland head coach Scott Bemand says their defeat against USA in the WXV Global Series opener at Tallaght Stadium was "a game we should have won".
items.titleTR: USA loss a game Ireland 'should have won' - Bemand

slots.packetSpot:
Ireland led the United States 31-12 for part of the second half in the opening match of the WXV Global Series at Tallaght Stadium. A comeback driven by four consecutive USA tries took the match to 40-36.

Head coach Scott Bemand said it was “a game we should have won”. Bemand stated that a loss of discipline in the second half and shortcomings in technical processes contributed to the defeat, and said the team needed to deliver stronger performances across the full 80 minutes.
slots.packetTitle: Ahead, then away

items.descriptionTR:
•	Former England player run over while warming up
	•	‘It turns out Stoke away wasn’t so bad,’ says winger 
The former England winger Andros Townsend has joked Stoke away “wasn’t so bad after all” following a bizarre incident in Thailand where he was run over by a pitch roller.
The former Tottenham and Crystal Palace attacker currently plays in Thai League 1 for PT Prachuap and made headlines on Saturday night when a clip emerged on social media which showed the 35-year-old being taken out before a fixture at Pattani.
items.titleTR: Andros Townsend avoids injury after bizarre pitch roller incident in Thailand

slots.packetSpot:
According to The Guardian, former England winger Andros Townsend, who plays for Thai League 1 side PT Prachuap, was knocked to the ground after being hit by a pitch roller while warming up before a match in Pattani. As an official in Pattani appeared to struggle to control the vehicle, Townsend’s left leg was briefly trapped beneath it.

The report says Townsend was not injured and came on as a substitute in Prachuap’s 3-0 win. The 35-year-old footballer took the incident in good humour on Instagram, referring to his earlier post about an away trip to Stoke.
slots.packetTitle: A joke on the pitch

items.descriptionTR:
Arizona State cantered to victory against Kansas in the first US college football game to be staged in the UK
You sensed that Britain’s first US college football game in nearly 40 years was going to be a very different experience when Wembley Way began to reverberate to the sound of steel, muscle and a few whoops long before kick-off.
The noise came from the Arizona State Sun Devils’ marching band, who were so energetic their horns and trombones swished from left to right like air raid lights hunting a target as they played. Soon there came a riposte from the Kansas Jayhawks’ marching band, along with more cheers from the large crowd outside the stadium.
items.titleTR: Union Jack Classic fails to spark on the pitch but electric atmosphere fires up Wembley

slots.packetSpot:
The American college football game held at Wembley for the first time created a strong fan atmosphere despite the uneven contest on the field. The report states that the Arizona State Sun Devils beat the Kansas Jayhawks 24-17, and that around 15,000 fans came from the United States for the game, watched by 46,523 people. Tailgate gatherings, marching bands, cheerleading displays, music and a light show brought the rituals of college football to London; however, the presentation was reportedly less spectacular than typical games in the United States.

Tickets were reportedly bought from 35 countries, with around 9,000 people supporting Arizona State and 6,000 supporting Kansas. It was also noted that more than 1,050 British coaches and referees received training during the year as part of the organisers’ ties with grassroots infrastructure in the United Kingdom. Following the exclusive multi-year agreement with Wembley, other Big 12 colleges are said to be interested in playing in London; an announcement for next year’s game is expected within one or two months.
slots.packetTitle: College football spills beyond the field at Wembley

items.descriptionTR: The couple spoke out for the first time since Lindsay Clancy's murder trial in an interview with BBC's US partner CBS.
items.titleTR: Watch: Patrick Clancy's new wife describes him as 'selfless father'

items.descriptionTR:
￼
Lindsay Clancy 's former husband said he forgave her for killing their three young children in his first televised interview Sunday on CBS News' 60 Minutes since a jury deadlocked in her trial for the children's deaths.
items.titleTR: Patrick Clancy gives first TV interview after Lindsay Clancy mistrial

slots.packetSpot:
Patrick Clancy and his new wife, Dr. Rachel Danis, spoke on television for the first time after the jury trial in Lindsay Clancy’s case over the deaths of their three children was declared a mistrial on September 4. In the interview aired on CBS News’s 60 Minutes, Patrick Clancy said he had forgiven Lindsay and believed the children’s deaths were linked to mental illness; he drew attention to perinatal mental health.

Patrick Clancy said he struggled with suicidal thoughts after the deaths and had a panic attack when the 911 call was played in court. He also stated that their youngest child, Callan, did not die immediately on the day of the incident, but died in his arms four days later. Cora and Dawson also died.

It was reported that 11 of the 12 jurors were prepared to find that Lindsay Clancy bore no criminal responsibility, while one juror sided with the prosecution. While the prosecution argued that Lindsay Clancy knew what she was doing, the majority believed she was experiencing postpartum psychosis. Rachel Danis described Patrick Clancy as a selfless and supportive husband; she said the story had been distorted. Patrick Clancy also said unfounded claims circulating on social media were harming his children’s legacy.
